newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha inches up on tight prompt supplies.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha inches up on tight prompt supplies.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were slightly firmer in afternoon Tokyo trade on Wednesday despite crude oil's losses on the ACCESS after-hours trading system, supported by tight availability for prompt cargoes, traders said.

Bids for first-half April open-specification naphtha were heard at $237.00 per tonne, while offers were notionally assessed $2.00 higher, compared with quotes of $237.00/238.00 in late trading on Monday. The Tokyo market was closed on Tuesday for a national holiday.
Second-half April was bid at $233.00 on Wednesday, with no offers having surfaced.
Most sellers remained on the sidelines, expecting a bullish naphtha market amid tight supplies, traders said.
In inter-month spreads the backwardation continued to steepen, with first-half April/first-half May indicated at plus $9.00/10.00.
Second-half April/second-half May was quoted at plus $8.00/9.00. On Monday, it was traded twice at plus $7.00.
Japan's kerosene demand was said to be slack due to this year's mild winter. Oil firms were expected to be able to satisfy most remaining winter demand from existing stocks.
